biography.value:
Intoxicated Rustclaws

During the celebration at the hideout, an intoxicated Rustclaw bruiser has disadvantage on its first attack roll and first saving throw during combat.
Mira avoids combat unless Pavo or another neighborhood resident is endangered.

Running Voss

Voss remains behind his troops and uses Tactical Order every round. He begins with Coordinated Volley when several characters have exposed themselves.
When reduced below half his hit points, Voss attempts to reach an Imperial transport or defensible command position. Capturing Tovan and recovering the NaviComputer remain more important to him than personally killing the characters.
Final Encounter Balance
For four 4th-level characters, begin with:

Commander Voss

2 stormtroopers
The security droid or environmental hazards
The other two stormtroopers should arrive as staggered reinforcements, typically during rounds 3 and 5.
Starting Voss beside four troopers and a security droid creates an extremely dangerous encounter, especially when the party must also protect the Stargazer and complete launch objectives.

Running Davik

Davik remains behind cover and coordinates allies. He prioritizes moving wounded crew members, protecting the Stargazer, and keeping escape routes open rather than personally pursuing enemies.

Running Tovan as an Ally
Tovan should protect the characters rather than replace them.
During the Imperial reconnaissance encounter, he normally does one of the following each round:
Uses Force Guidance
Heals an injured character
Pushes enemies away from a wounded pilot
Deflects an incoming blaster shot
Holds open an escape route
He draws his lightsaber only when the characters or civilians are in immediate danger. Once he does, the Empire receives confirmation that a Jedi is present unless the characters prevent all transmissions.

Running Ressik

Ressik begins by challenging a visibly powerful character to single combat. He uses Hook and Hurl to throw opponents from platforms or into machinery.
The other Rustclaws lose confidence when Ressik is bloodied. If Ressik falls, surviving gang members should surrender or flee rather than continue a prolonged battle.

Encounter Balance

For four 2nd-level characters:
Ressik alone: Hard encounter
Ressik and one gang fighter: Hard to deadly
Ressik, one bruiser, and two fighters: Deadly boss encounter
Entire hideout simultaneously: Overwhelming and inappropriate
The characters should be able to isolate Ressik, sabotage the hideout, turn gang members against him, or prevent reinforcements from reaching his hall.

Running the Security Droid
The droid remains beside an Imperial officer or important objective. It restrains mobile characters, blocks narrow passages, and uses Concussive Pulse when surrounded.
For the final hangar encounter, the security droid should arrive with Commander Voss and two stormtroopers, while additional troops enter later as reinforcements.

biography.value:
Running Tensin

Tensin fights only when cornered. He uses his smoke capsule immediately after taking significant damage and attempts to escape with information, valuables, or whichever bargaining chip is closest.

Running the Investigator
The investigator prefers detention and interrogation over killing. It uses stormtroopers as protection, marks dangerous characters, and retreats if isolated.

Intoxicated Rustclaws

During the celebration at the hideout, an intoxicated Rustclaw fighter has disadvantage on its first attack roll and first saving throw during combat.

description.value:
The Freighter shudders with the blasts of cannon fire. Despite its maneuvers, the pilot can't quite shake the pursuit. The technician's efforts to reinforce the shields are failing. The mechanic is pumping the reactor for every scrap of energy it can generate. The operator is frantically making the final few calculations for the jump to hyperspace. Finally, just as the ship's shields dissipate, the pilot makes the gut call, jettisoning the illicit cargo. As it distracts and hampers the followers, the freighter shifts power to the thrusters and quickly flies away.

As the pirates activate their tractor beam to attempt to capture the weaponless frigate and its exotic wares, the gunboat escort intercedes. It flies in the line of the tractor, breaking the lock on the frigate, and unleashes a volley of cannon fire. The pirates, incapable of withstanding the salvo, drop the tractor beam and retreat.

As the gunboat pursues to be sure the pirates don't come back for a second bite at the apple, the crew finally locks on target and unleashes a long-range night-stinger missile, putting a permanent end to the pirates' illicit and unwelcome activities.

The captain invites his guests into his well-stocked cantina. He eyes the opposition as they take in his ship, assessing their reactions and noting their expressions. Fully aware of the effect the opulent room has on the unprepared, he easily stifles his grin and gestures for the starry-eyed vis-itors to sit across from him. He indicates for the server to bring drinks as he casually leans back and puts his feet on the table, confident this deal will go his way. He presses a button on the tiny remote in his hand, causing hidden panels to slide away and reveal his mostly-legal wares. "So," he says, "just how many of these do you need, and where will I deliver them?"

Medium ships are the bread and butter of the closeknit group. They are large enough to accommodate all of the immediate needs of a crew, while at the same time being small enough to feel cozy.

Lightweight armor is commonly used on smaller ships, allowing them to take full advantage of their quickness.
Direct power coupling has a central power capacitor that feeds power directly to each system.

The hyperdrive is a propulsion system that allows a starship to reach hyperspeed and traverse the void between stars in the alternate dimension of hyperspace. For a starship to have a hyperdrive, it must have a vacant hyperdrive slot modification.
Fuel cell reactors are the most common and balanced reactors on the market.

Ranged Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, range 80/320 ft. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
Orra and companions traveling with her cannot become lost through nonmagical or non-Force means while she remains conscious.
Orra takes the Help action, assisting a creature with a Perception, Investigation, or Survival check. The assisted creature can be up to 30 feet away if it can hear Orra.
When a creature within 5 feet of the bruiser attacks one of the bruiser’s allies, the bruiser can use its reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll.
The bruiser makes two [[/item Shock Maul]] attacks.
The bruiser has advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to resist being pushed, pulled, knocked &Reference[Prone apply=false], or forcibly moved.
Ranged Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
Melee Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
One creature within 10 feet that can hear the bruiser must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or have disadvantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn.
The bruiser makes one [[/item Shock Maul]] attack. On a hit, the target must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 10 feet and knocked &Reference[Prone apply=false].
Melee Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
When an allied creature within 5 feet is targeted by an attack, Mira imposes disadvantage on the attack roll.
Melee Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
Pavo can use an action to disable one unattended mundane machine or vehicle component. Restoring it requires an action and a successful DC 12 Technology check.
Pavo repairs a droid, vehicle, or unattended machine he can touch, restoring 7 ([[/r 2d6]]) hit points. Alternatively, he can grant advantage on the next Technology check made to repair that machine.
Voss has advantage on saving throws against being &Reference[Charmed apply=false] or &Reference[Frightened apply=false].
Imperial allies within 30 feet of Voss that can hear him gain a +2 bonus to Wisdom saving throws and weapon damage rolls.
Voss has advantage on initiative rolls and cannot be surprised while he is conscious.
Ranged Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.

When Voss is hit by an attack and an allied Imperial creature is within 5 feet, Voss exchanges places with that creature. The allied creature becomes the target of the attack instead. Voss cannot use this reaction against an area effect or if the allied creature is &Reference[Incapacitated apply=false].
Voss makes one [[/item Precision Blaster Pistol]] attack. He then chooses up to two Imperial allies within 60 feet that can hear him. Each chosen ally may use its reaction to make one weapon attack.
Melee Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage, and the target cannot take reactions until the beginning of its next turn.

Voss throws a grenade at a point within 40 feet. Each creature within 10 feet of that point must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 7 ([[/r 2d6]]) sonic damage and is &Reference[Blinded apply=false] until the end of its next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and is not &Reference[Blinded apply=false].
Voss makes two attacks with his precision blaster pistol or command baton.
Voss chooses one Imperial ally within 30 feet. The target either moves up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks or takes the Dodge action.
Davik chooses one allied creature within 30 feet that can hear him. That creature can use its reaction to move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks or make one weapon attack.
Davik can take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action as a bonus action.
Davik makes two attacks with his modified heavy blaster or vibrodagger.
Ranged Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
When Davik fails an ability check or saving throw, he can roll a d6 and add it to the result, potentially turning the failure into a success.
Davik has advantage on Charisma checks involving smugglers, mechanics, black-market merchants, or planetary criminals who recognize his name.
Melee Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
Davik reduces the damage dealt to him by one attack by 7 ([[/r 1d8 + 3]]).
Tovan touches one creature, which regains 12 ([[/r 2d8 + 3]]) hit points. This ability has no effect on droids or constructs.

When Tovan takes energy damage from a ranged weapon attack, he reduces the damage by 12 ([[/r 1d10 + 7]]). If this reduces the damage to 0 and the attacker is within 60 feet, Tovan may redirect the shot. He makes a ranged force attack with a +7 bonus. On a hit, the attacker takes 7 (1d6 + 4) energy damage.
Tovan chooses one creature he can see within 30 feet. That creature adds [[/r 1d4]] to the next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw it makes before the beginning of Tovan’s next turn.
Tovan’s damaged lightsaber is dangerous to use for prolonged periods. If he rolls a natural 1 on a lightsaber attack, the weapon deactivates and cannot be used until the end of his next turn.
Tovan makes two lightsaber attacks. He avoids using this action unless someone under his protection is in immediate danger.

Tovan releases a wave of Force energy in a 15-foot cone. Each creature of his choice in that area must make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 10 ([[/r 3d6]]) kinetic damage, is pushed up to 15 feet, and falls &Reference[Prone apply=false]. On a success, it takes half damage and is not pushed or knocked &Reference[Prone apply=false].

Tovan is a 5th-level forcecaster. His forcecasting ability is Wisdom; his force save DC is 15, and he has +7 to hit with force attacks. Tovan has 18 force points and typically employs nonlethal or defensive powers.
When Tovan reduces a creature to 0 hit points with a melee attack, he may choose to render the creature &Reference[Unconscious apply=false] and stable.
Tovan cannot be surprised while conscious. He has advantage on initiative rolls and Wisdom checks made to detect living creatures or imminent danger.
Melee Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
Opportunity attacks made by Ressik have advantage.
Melee Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
Ressik moves up to half his speed toward his Worthy Prey. This movement does not provoke an opportunity attack from that creature.

Ressik makes a [[/item Trophy Vibro-Axe]] attack. On a hit, the target must succeed on a DC 14 Strength saving throw or be thrown up to 10 feet, land &Reference[Prone apply=false], and take an additional 7 ([[/r 2d6]]) kinetic damage.
If Ressik is reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, he drops to 1 hit point instead.
Ranged Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, range 50/200 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
Ressik makes two attacks, only one of which can be made with his heavy blaster pistol.
Ressik adds 3 to his AC against one melee attack that would hit him. Ressik must see the attacker and be wielding his vibro-axe.
Melee Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
Ressik is immune to the &Reference[Poisoned apply=false] condition when it results from alcohol or recreational intoxicants. He suffers no penalties from the Rustclaws’ celebration.

At the beginning of combat, Ressik selects one creature he can see. Once on each of his turns, Ressik deals an additional 3 ([[/r 1d6]]) damage when he hits that creature. Ressik invariably chooses a Wookiee when one is present, but the feature otherwise functions identically.
Creatures provoke opportunity attacks from the droid even when they take the Disengage action.
The droid is immune to effects that would alter its form.
The droid has advantage on initiative rolls and cannot be surprised while powered.
Melee Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.

Each creature within 10 feet of the droid must make a DC 13 Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 9 ([[/r 2d8]]) sonic damage, is pushed 10 feet, and falls &Reference[Prone apply=false]. On a successful save, it takes half damage and is not pushed or knocked &Reference[Prone apply=false].

Ranged Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, range 20/40 ft., one Large or smaller creature. On a hit, the target is &Reference[Grappled apply=false]. The escape DC is 13. Until the grapple ends, the target is &Reference[Restrained apply=false], and the droid cannot use its restraint cable against another target. The cable has AC 14 and 10 hit points.
Ranged Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
When a creature within 5 feet of the droid attacks an Imperial officer, the droid imposes disadvantage on the attack roll.
The droid makes two attacks: two armored fist attacks, or one armored fist attack and one integrated blaster attack.
The security droid does not require air, food, drink, or sleep.
Tensin can take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action as a bonus action.

Tensin deals an extra 3 ([[/r 1d6]]) damage when he hits a target with a weapon attack and has advantage on the attack roll, or when an ally of Tensin is within 5 feet of the target and Tensin does not have disadvantage.

Tensin throws a capsule at a point within 20 feet. A 10-foot-radius sphere centered on that point becomes heavily obscured until the end of Tensin’s next turn. Tensin may immediately move up to half his speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
When an attack misses Tensin, he can move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.
Ranged Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, range 40/160 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
Tensin has advantage on ability checks made to locate exits, hidden passages, crowds, or other possible escape routes.
Melee Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
One Imperial ally within 30 feet that can hear the investigator can move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.
If the investigator has not moved during its turn, its first ranged weapon attack that turn deals an additional 3 ([[/r 1d6]]) damage on a hit.
After observing a creature for at least 1 minute, the investigator has advantage on its next Insight or Investigation check concerning that creature.
When a creature the investigator can see makes a Deception or Stealth check, the investigator adds 3 to its passive Perception or passive Insight against that check.
Melee Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage, and the target cannot take reactions until the beginning of its next turn.
Ranged Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
The investigator has advantage on Charisma checks made against Imperial personnel of lower rank and civilians who fear Imperial retaliation.

The investigator identifies one creature it can see within 60 feet. Until the beginning of the investigator’s next turn, Imperial allies have advantage on the first attack roll they make against that creature.

One electronic device or droid within 30 feet must make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it takes 9 ([[/r 2d8]]) ion damage and cannot take reactions until the end of its next turn. Keelo surrenders when reduced below half his hit points or when threatened with Imperial arrest.

Keelo targets one electronic device within 60 feet that he can access wirelessly or through a connected terminal. He can perform one of the following: Lock or unlock a door Deactivate a light or camera Trigger a local alarm Give one creature advantage or disadvantage on its next Technology check involving the system

Sella fires toward a point within 60 feet. Creatures of her choice within 10 feet of that point must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or have disadvantage on attack rolls until the beginning of Sella’s next turn.
Sella makes two [[/item Light Blaster]] attacks.
Sella can Dash, Disengage, or Hide as a bonus action.
Ranged Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, range 40/160 ft. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
The fighter has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the fighter’s allies is within 5 feet of the creature and is not &Reference[Incapacitated apply=false].
The fighter takes the Help action to assist an ally attacking a creature within 5 feet. The fighter can then move up to 10 feet without provoking an opportunity attack from that creature.
When the fighter begins its turn with 5 or fewer hit points and no conscious Rustclaw leader is within 30 feet, it must succeed on a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw or attempt to flee or surrender.

Melee Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.

A character offering a plausible excuse, minor bribe, or completed document has advantage on checks made to convince Harven not to investigate further. Harven immediately surrenders if seriously threatened.
Ranged Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, range 40/160 ft. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage.
Harven has advantage on Charisma checks made against low-ranking Imperial personnel while issuing routine bureaucratic instructions.
Ranged Weapon Attack: [[/attack]] to hit, range 30/120 ft. Hit: [[/damage average]] damage. A creature reduced to 0 hit points by this attack is &Reference[Unconscious apply=false] and stable.
Halden can stabilize a dying creature as a bonus action.
Halden touches a living creature and restores 8 ([[/r 1d8 + 4]]) hit points.
